title: From Self-driving to Autonomous Voice Agents — Brooke Hopkins, Coval
talk_summary: Brooke Hopkins (Coval, ex-Waymo) argues that large-scale simulation and continuous eval loops—not brittle hand-written scenario tests—are what made self-driving reliable, and applies the same playbook to voice agents. Key mechanisms: reference-free probabilistic metrics, denoising flaky failures by re-running scenarios many times, and calibrating LLM-as-judge against a small human-labeled set.

takeaways.technique: Denoise flaky failures by re-running the scenario N times
takeaways.what_they_do: When an eval fails once, they re-simulate that same scenario ~100 times to measure the failure probability rather than treating a single failure as a defect.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you reimulate that a hundred times. So is this scenario failing 50 out of a 100 times? Is it a coin flip?

takeaways.technique: Calibrate LLM-as-judge against a small human-labeled set
takeaways.what_they_do: They iterate the automated metric until it correlates with human feedback on ~10-100 labeled examples, then trust it at 10,000-scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: iterate over and over until your automated metrics are aligning with human feedback. And now you have the confidence to go deploy those

takeaways.technique: Reference-free probabilistic metrics over golden-output matching
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asserting exact expected outputs per input, they define aggregate metrics (how often does it resolve, repeat, say wrong things) that apply across many scenarios.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reference free evaluation where you don't necessarily need to say these are all of the expected things

takeaways.technique: Tiered eval pyramid: cheap text-level first, full end-to-end last
takeaways.what_they_do: They test workflows/tool-calls/instruction-following in text (fast/cheap), reserve voice-to-voice for latency/interruption, and hyperrealistic audio only for reproducing production issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: doing that all with text is probably the fastest and cheapest way to do that

takeaways.technique: Continuous eval loop wired into CI/CD + live monitoring feedback
takeaways.what_they_do: Bug found → reproduce with eval → fix → run larger regression set → presubmit/postsubmit CI → release gate → live monitoring feeds back into the test suite.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I fix the issue and then I run more... then you run a larger regression set, make sure you didn't break everything

takeaways.technique: Scope small, don't over-automate; keep humans on judgment calls
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly do not try to automate all evals—automation for speed/scale, humans for judgment—and scope a smaller problem rather than automating everything at once.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The goal is not to automate all evals, but rather to leverage auto evals for speed and scale
